title: Amazon’s Best New Kindle Offering Is a $35 Accessory
gist: A Wired review of the $35 Amazon Kindle Click, a Bluetooth page-turner compatible with 2024 and 2026 Kindles, which the author calls the best buy in Amazon's new Kindle lineup. The piece also compares costs with the $80 page-turn case and Kobo's Libra Colour.

insights.claim: Amazon's Kindle Click is a $35 Bluetooth remote that turns pages, scrolls and adjusts brightness, and works with 2024 and 2026 Kindles.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Cheap accessory extends hardware ecosystem value.

insights.claim: The Click improves on third-party page turners, which typically required a screen-blocking clip plus a separate remote, each needing its own charging.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell

insights.claim: The Click is positioned as an accessibility aid for people who cannot comfortably hold a device and tap pages.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Accessibility use cases widen the addressable audience.

insights.claim: Battery life is only specified as lasting weeks, and the Click ships weeks after launch, so supply is tight ahead of the holidays.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Holiday-quarter demand outstripping supply for a minor product.

insights.claim: Amazon's new page-turn case costs $80 and requires a Kindle Signature Edition starting at $250, bringing the cost to $330, or about $400 with the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Amazon's physical-button route is priced above rival Kobo.

insights.claim: The author argues buyers wanting physical page-turn buttons should choose Kobo's Libra Colour at $258, saving around $75 compared with Kindle plus case.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Kobo is price-competitive in premium color e-readers.
insights.quote: go buy a Kobo Libra Colour ($258)

insights.claim: The author expects 2024 Kindle models to go on sale for Black Friday, but has little hope that the newest models will be discounted yet.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Newest Amazon hardware holds price into the holiday season.
